skills.name: benchmarking

skills.name: build

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline

skills.name: coding-standards

skills.name: daemon-development

skills.name: gdb-debugging

skills.name: kernel-development

skills.name: library-development

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development

skills.name: pptx
skills.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates, layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.

skills.name: ast-consistency
skills.description: AST-level exec fidelity checking tools and pre-approved deviations. Use after modifying source files to verify exec code is unchanged.

skills.name: body-removal
skills.description: Remove function bodies from Rust/Verus source files to produce signature-only views. Used before the view-design phase to prevent implementation anchoring.

skills.name: bug-reporting
skills.description: Classify and report bugs found during Verus verification. Distinguishes true bugs from missing constraints and verifier limitations. Use when a verification failure might indicate a code bug.

skills.name: caller-analysis
skills.description: Analyze callers of a Rust module to understand usage expectations for Verus verification. Produces a caller-perspective analysis covering all functions with their visibility and call relationships.

skills.name: crate-analysis
skills.description: Principles for verification order in multi-file Rust crates. Verify top-level modules first (top-down), writing dependency specs on demand as verification drills down. The pipeline tool handles ordering automatically.

skills.name: proof-extraction
skills.description: Extract large inline proof blocks from exec code into named lemmas in .proof.rs. Use when polishing verified code to improve readability and proof organization.

skills.name: proof-minimization
skills.description: Remove redundant proof artifacts (assertions, lemmas, hints, dead code) without weakening guarantees. Use when polishing verified code to reduce verbosity.

skills.name: property-analysis
skills.description: How to analyze source code and identify verification properties — the WHAT of verification. Covers module understanding, property discovery across four dimensions (functional correctness, safety, liveness, structural consistency), and quality review. Use this skill when deciding what to verify for a new module, writing property_analysis.md, or updating global_properties.md.

skills.name: proving-guide
skills.description: Proving methodology and mindset for Verus verification: function-by-function approach, persistence through failures, clean verification, and bug reporting. Use when writing proofs or resolving verification failures.

skills.name: review-methodology
skills.description: Review Verus verification code with focus on spec quality and automated checks.

skills.name: spec-completeness
skills.description: Detect specification incompleteness via nondeterminism checking. Given a Verus function spec, automatically determine whether the spec uniquely determines the output for each valid input. If not, use type-guided binary search to construct a concrete witness (input + two valid but different outputs). No LLM needed — pure SMT-based.

skills.name: spec-design
skills.description: How to write good Verus specs. Covers spec quality principles (anti-patterns, error paths), spec classification (internal, external-top, external-bottom trust boundaries), View abstraction design, and static vs dynamic enforcement. Use when writing or reviewing Verus specs.

skills.name: verification-order
skills.description: Determine function-level verification order within a module using the verification plan. Use at the start of proving to know which function to verify first and how to sequence work.

skills.name: verus-constraints
skills.description: Mandatory rules for writing Verus code. Covers attribute-based syntax, source integrity for exec code, forbidden patterns, and assume_specification policy. Must be followed whenever producing or modifying Verus-annotated code.

skills.name: verus-setup
skills.description: Set up Verus formal verification infrastructure for a Rust project. Covers workspace-level config (vstd dependency, cfg flags, version pinning, Makefile, scripts) and per-crate config (metadata, cfg-gated includes, spec/proof stubs). Use this skill when preparing a repo or crate for Verus verification, adding make verify support, or integrating cheating detection into a build.

skills.name: verus-syntax
skills.description: Verus attribute-based syntax reference for exec functions. Covers #[verus_spec], #[verus_verify], proof!{}, proof_decl!{}, loop invariants. See GUIDE.md for advanced patterns, syntax_attr.rs for the official example.

skills.name: view-design
skills.description: How to design a View type that represents abstract state from the caller's perspective. Input: caller analysis + property concepts. Must NOT see implementation code.

8. ## 1. `ExFrameNumber` external_type_specification
9. 
10. - **File:** `frame.spec.rs:10-12`
11. - **Trust item:** `#[verifier::external_type_specification]` + `#[verifier::external_body]`
12. - **Classification:** `EXTERNAL_TYPE`
13. - **Justification:** `FrameNumber` is defined in the `arch` crate. Verus needs a
14.   type specification to reason about it. The type itself is a newtype wrapper
15.   around `usize` in the arch crate; its internal representation is opaque to the
16.   kernel verification scope.
17. - **Reproducer:** N/A — external_type_specification is the standard mechanism
18.   for bringing external types into Verus scope.

24. - **File:** `frame.spec.rs:18-23`
25. - **Trust item:** `assume_specification` on `::arch::mem::FRAME_SIZE`
26. - **Classification:** `EXTERNAL_CONST`
27. - **Justification:** `FRAME_SIZE` is a constant defined in the `arch` crate
28.   (value = 4096). Verus cannot evaluate external constants. The spec asserts
29.   `result == spec_page_size()`, `result > 0`, and `result >= 2`, which match
30.   the actual constant value.
31. - **Reproducer:** Verus cannot resolve constants from external crates without
32.   `assume_specification`.

41. - **Justification:** Wraps `self_.into_frame_number().into_raw_value()` — a
42.   method chain on `FrameAddress` (a `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>`) that
43.   involves generic `Deref` trait dispatch. Verus cannot express
44.   `assume_specification` on generic trait methods (`Deref::deref` for
